completed_stage_receipts.summary: Confirmed a control-plane state-drift defect: the user explicitly reports deleting the Continuity monitors and current product-state reread shows the declared core monitor tasks absent, while durable/rebuildable repository surfaces still claim them enabled or hourly-active. The user deletion is intentional product mutation; the defect is stale repository liveness representation, not the deletion itself.

Initial failure class was external-product-observation-staleness. Validation subsequently exposed a second systemic class: task manifest mutation version is incorrectly coupled to latest completed formal meta-maintenance proof version, even though legal lease takeover independently increments manifest_version.

Expanded the impact map: live external monitor state -> repository liveness snapshot plus task manifest mutation/CAS version -> lease takeover version increments -> latest completed formal meta-run binding -> CI closure guard. BUSINESS state remains out of scope. The proof-binding conflict can fail every legitimate manifest version advance that is not itself a new formal meta-maintenance run.

reopen_history.reason: Hosted CI run 38275331371 failed because compacting the manifest removed a required methodology contract field; implementation was reopened and the field restored.

Second hosted CI run 38275584909 proved a deeper pre-existing architecture conflict: runtime/universal_continuity.py legally increments manifest_version on every resume takeover, while tests/test_meta_maintenance.py requires the latest completed formal meta-run target_manifest_version to equal the current manifest_version. The current handoff explicitly keeps the latest formal run at V61, so ordinary takeover/status mutation and formal proof lifecycle are incorrectly coupled.
